title: [FMLA 22] StadiaHeight — Stadia Calculations (Height)
formulas: H = K s sinθ cosθ + C sinθ
H = (1/2) K s sin(2θ) + C sinθ
summary: Surveying stadia elevation difference from staff interval s and elevation angle θ (Deg), with instrument constants K and C.

body.text: Calculator scroll name: StadiaHeight. Elevation difference from the transit to the leveling rod, using the staff interval s between the stadia hairs and the angle of elevation θ.
Surveying: look through the instrument at a vertical staff. K and C are instrument constants; s and θ are what you read.

body.caption: Sight onto a staff. The interval s between the two stadia hairs, with elevation angle θ, is turned into elevation difference h = Ks sinθ cosθ + C sinθ.

body.text: Primary inputs: K, s, C, θ.

body.title: How to run
items: Press FMLA, then 2, then 2 (or scroll to the name and EXE)
Enter stadia constant K, interval s, additive C, angle θ
Height H = Ks sinθ cosθ + C sinθ

body.label: Angle unit
body.text: Run in Deg. Typical internal-focus instruments use K = 100 and C = 0. Companion distance formula is FMLA 23: D = Ks cos²θ + C cosθ.
